subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should exhausted context overflow stay compaction-only, or may OpenClaw route the same turn to a larger configured fallback model?
rationale: The remaining work changes core failover semantics and can affect replay safety, model-selection guarantees, and documented user recovery behavior.

options.title: Implement guarded larger-context fallback
options.body: After compaction/truncation is exhausted, retry only on candidates with a proven larger effective context window and a safe replay boundary.

options.title: Keep compaction-only policy
options.body: Leave fallback excluded for overflow and strengthen docs/error recovery around `/compact`, `/reset`, and `/new`.

options.title: Defer to adjacent UX work
options.body: Keep this issue open until related overflow diagnostics and model-switch recovery work settle the user-facing recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Implement guarded larger-context fallback
recommendation.body: After compaction/truncation is exhausted, retry only on candidates with a proven larger effective context window and a safe replay boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history touches the fallback classifier and source-contract alignment around the affected behavior.
